claim_text: The wavy deformation bands are deformation kink bands: their crystal rotation angle varies continuously from ~5 to ~55 deg instead of taking the fixed ~85 deg of {10-12} twins

steps.observation: OM of the [11-20] and [01-10] specimens: straight {10-12}/{01-12} band traces plus wavy bands whose contrast is strong on the (0001) side surface and faint on (1-100)/(-2110)
steps.image_note: the band and trace-plane labels are written on the panels; the contrast asymmetry between the two side surfaces is a pixel judgement (dark wavy bands in (c) and (e), faint in (d) and (f))

steps.contribution_why: The OM observation morphologically distinguishes wavy bands (asymmetric surface contrast) from straight {10-12}/{01-12} twin traces, supporting that they are a distinct deformation mode, but it provides no crystallographic orientation/rotation-angle data needed to establish the specific 5-55 deg continuous rotation versus the fixed ~85 deg twin rotation.
unsettled: quantitative crystal rotation angle of wavy bands
confirmation of fixed ~85 deg rotation for {10-12} twins
identification of wavy bands as kink bands specifically rather than another non-twin feature

steps.observation: Where wavy bands form, the (1-100)/(-2110) side surface develops a step-like ridge (red arrows) while the (0001) surface stays straight, so the band shear direction is parallel to [0001]
steps.image_note: red arrows mark the ridge; the (0001) views of the same specimens keep a straight outline, which is what makes the shear direction readable

steps.contribution_why: The surface step/ridge morphology showing shear parallel to [0001] supports a kink-band deformation mechanism (consistent with slip-induced shear) but does not itself measure or pin down the specific crystal rotation angle range (~5 to ~55 deg) or contrast it against the fixed ~85 deg twin rotation.

comparison to fixed ~85 deg {10-12} twin rotation
continuous variation of rotation angle across the band

steps.image_note: the green 'basal plane trace' polyline and the red arrows are drawn on the panel; the varying bend angle along that polyline is the pixel reading

steps.contribution_why: The TEM trace-bending observation shows non-constant boundary angles and confirms many low-angle (<15 deg) boundaries exist, which supports the kink-band interpretation and contradicts a single fixed ~85 deg twin angle, but it does not itself quantify the full continuous range up to ~55 deg or establish that the variation spans exactly ~5-55 deg.
unsettled: continuity of the angle distribution across the full 5-55 deg range
